## Notes

* **N1 — a seam between the limit's value and the kernel's work limit (session ruling needed; CONFIRMED by a probe,
  the consequence PLAUSIBLE).** C-0174 (6) chooses "no rounding" and `law.ts` 45 calls the value "the value a stage
  passes as `KernelTx.workLimit` (§3.3)". The kernel's landed consumers take only whole numbers: `insertTx` asserts
  `check(Number.isInteger(workLimit) && workLimit >= 0, 'a work limit is a whole number of operations')`
  (`kernel/src/insert/classes.ts` 129), and `skeleton` silently drops a non-integer `maxEvents`
  (`skeleton/skeleton.ts` 86: `asked !== undefined && Number.isInteger(asked) && asked > floor ? asked : floor`). The
  probe `scratchpad/waves/chk-f03a-seam.mts` printed: `growth.proposals at 0.37 ha -> 4190.72 integer? false`; a
  p999 × 1.5 coefficient (`perUnit 10.5`) at 3 faces `-> 4127.5`; `insertTx refused: insert: a work limit is a whole
  number of operations`. Today only the `landHa` laws give fractions; after M0-f-03b writes p999 × 1.5 coefficients
  nearly every law will. The two items also state opposite edges: C-0174 (6) "a count reaches the limit when ≥ it"
  (§5.1 (5)'s "reaches"), while `charge` allows `total <= workLimit` and the skeleton stops at `events > limit`
  (§3.3's "exceeds"). No choices row records the kernel's whole-number rule (a grep of `choices.md` for "whole
  number" finds none). One owner should decide before M0-f-03b and M0-a-06's `KernelTx`: either `workLimitOf` returns
  ⌊limit⌋ (operations are whole; a new row superseding C-0174 (6)'s rounding clause and its edge sentence), or the
  kernel accepts any finite limit ≥ 0 (a row for M0-a-04 / M0-a-11 / M0-a-06). Not a failing line of this item: the
  design states neither rounding nor the edge, and C-0174 declares its choice.
* **N2 — `warp.halvings`'s floor is test-pinned yet marked calibratable (CONFIRMED; consequence PLAUSIBLE).** The cell
  reads `"floor": {"value": 8, …, "provenance": "architecture 2026-10-03 placeholder", "calibratable": true}`, so the
  census counts it (33) and M1's register check will treat it as calibratable, while `table.test.ts` 178 pins it to 8
  at every version and §3.6 states "at most 8 halvings". C-0174 (1) – (2) declare the layout, so this is no deviation;
  the honest form is `architecture 2026-10-03`, `calibratable: false` (census 32, the placeholder test excepting the
  fixed row). Recommended to the session for the fix round or M0-f-03b's hand-over.
* **N3 — the memory rule's example command does not pass its flags (CONFIRMED for the file set).** The root script is
  `vitest run`, so `corepack pnpm test -- --project tables --maxWorkers=2` reached vitest as `vitest run -- --project
  tables --maxWorkers=2` and ran all 163 files; `--project` was ignored, and by the same parse `--maxWorkers=2` was too
  (PLAUSIBLE; memory stayed at 73 % free). `corepack pnpm exec vitest run --project tables --maxWorkers=2 …` applies
  both (11 files). J168's brief text gives the first form as its example.
* **N4 — the record's wave label (CONFIRMED).** The record is against wave-4, as `landed.mjs`'s `--wave` text allows;
  the wave-4 close (fedb216) held the item's nine files and record out, and the wave-6f snapshot (19:28 UTC) already
  holds their bytes, so `landed:verify -- wave-6f` sees 0 records and 0 changes from this item. The steward staging
  wave 6f must take the item's files from this wave-4 record (they are untracked or modified against HEAD). The fix
  round's own record, against the open wave, will list them as unchanged.
